items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: In fact I was talking to Howard about it.

ctx.x: My feeling is everybody says at these jazz parties everybody’s white haired in the audience and everything, and do you think there’s a future, and I say well I think if we’re lucky we’ll all die off at the same time. And it will all go with the audience. But then Harry says well thanks a lot. And I actually sometimes, I don’t know, I mean people say that but I’m glad I’m at the age I am. I don’t think I’d want to be 25 and liking the music

that I like and trying to make a living at it. I’m a pessimist enough to think that if Frank Sinatra were starting out singing now, he’d have a hell of a time getting a job, because of the climate of the times and the kind of music that’s popular. So I don’t know. All I know is I’m 52 and maybe I could eke out a living for another 25 years. But I mean certainly it’s going on in the schools, which I think there’s a pro and con to that. I think that like classical music, when it got institutionalized, I don’t think…

It sounds like a great idea and to have people teaching that are professional players. Because I think sometimes the students are being taught by teachers who have just been teachers. And that they are great players themselves, but as you say, they might not know the songs enough themselves that they can pass it on. I guess there’s less venues to play and sometimes I think we don’t need more players, we need more audience.
